data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's proposed distinguishing evidence (Trigger-Response Distribution / Poisson-vs-bursty delta) is not sufficient for the problem's evidentiary requirement. A hidden shared cause that triggers failures intermittently and at low rate can produce a failure process whose inter-arrival times are statistically indistinguishable from a homogeneous Poisson process over any finite observation window. In that case the 'bursty' signature is absent, so the proposed test would classify the failures as truly independent when they are in fact pseudo-uncorrelated. The target even acknowledges this gap as a countercondition (shared trigger mimicking Poisson) but still states the distinction 'is revealed' by the Poisson-vs-bursty delta, which the countercondition directly refutes.
